title: Sport — Wednesday Sport & Representative Sport
exam_focus: Uses real school sport materials as the setting: sport knowledge, rules, competition progression rules, sport safety and first aid, fitness training principles (progressive overload) and healthy living. Moderate difficulty.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of a warm-up before a training session or trial?
options: To use up energy so you do not get tired later in the session
To raise heart rate and muscle temperature and lower injury risk
To replace the need for a cool-down at the end of the session
To build muscle size quickly before the session starts
questions.explanation_en: The core of warming up is to gradually increase heart rate, muscle temperature, and joint mobility, letting the body enter the exercise state and reduce the risk of pulling a muscle, it cannot replace relaxation, and is not used to 'consume energy'.
questions.source: Bally Volleyball（7:30am warm up before the 8:00am trial）

questions.topic: Ball sport rules · Volleyball team size
questions.stem: In indoor volleyball, how many players from each team are on the court at one time?
questions.explanation_en: Indoor volleyball has 6 players on each team on the court, with rotation for serving, 2 players are for beach volleyball, 11 players are for football/cricket etc., don't mix them up.
questions.source: Bally Volleyball (indoor volleyball team) + syllabus knowledge

questions.stem: How many players are on each team in beach volleyball?
questions.explanation_en: Beach volleyball has 2 players on each team, the court is smaller but there's no rotation for substitution, indoor volleyball is the one with 6 players on each team.
questions.source: Bally Volleyball (2021 indoor and beach teams) + syllabus knowledge

questions.stem: According to the Sydney North rugby league permission note, which piece of protective equipment is mandatory in all games and training sessions?
options: A correctly fitted mouthguard
Shin pads worn under the socks
A padded scrum cap for the head
Knee strapping on both legs
questions.explanation_en: The consent form explicitly states that 'wearing suitable mouthguards in all games and training is compulsory' to reduce teeth and facial injuries, shin guards and knee pads are not compulsory equipment for this sport.

questions.stem: At the Balgowlah Boys Athletics Carnival, which athletes are expected to compete at the North Shore Athletics Carnival?
options: Everyone who finishes the race on the day
The top two finishers in each age group
Only the winner of each individual event
The fastest ten runners in each age group
questions.explanation_en: The athletics carnival rules state that the top two in each age group will enter the North Shore carnival, the top 'ten' is the qualifying standard for cross-country, don't mix up the rules for the two events.
questions.source: Bally Boys school athletics carnival permission note.doc（Zone Representation）

questions.stem: To qualify for the Zone cross country team, a runner must:
options: Finish in the top ten of their age group
Finish in the top two of their age group
Complete the course under 15 minutes
Be selected by the sports captain
questions.explanation_en: Cross-country takes the top ten in each age group to enter the Zone team, with a wider threshold than athletics' top two, these two numbers are the easiest to set traps in the exam.
questions.source: School XC Program 2025 - amended.docx（Guidelines — To qualify for Zone）

questions.stem: At the swimming carnival, the fastest two swimmers normally qualify for the Zone carnival. For which event does only the fastest swimmer qualify?
options: 50m Freestyle
100m Butterfly
50m Breaststroke
4 x 50m Relay
questions.explanation_en: Only the fastest time is taken for 200m freestyle, 200m individual medley, and 100m butterfly, the top two are taken for other events, 50m freestyle takes the top two and the next two form a relay team.

questions.stem: A boy finishes third in the 50m Freestyle in his age group at the school swimming carnival. Which statement is correct?
options: He qualifies for the Zone carnival because the top three in each event go through
He misses Zone in that event but may still make the age relay as a fastest four
He automatically becomes age champion because he finished in the top three
He must swim a final race against the other placegetters to decide the result
questions.explanation_en: For 50m freestyle, only the top two will enter the Zone, the third won't; but 'the top four in each age group for 50m freestyle will form an age relay team', so the third may still be selected for the relay, also all events are ranked by time, with no finals.
questions.source: Swimming Carnival Program 2020 (3).pdf（Zone qualifiers / Age Relay Team）

questions.stem: The Wednesday Sport program only increases the running load slightly each week (for example walk 5 / jog 0, then jog 1 / walk 4, then jog 3 / walk 2). Why does it progress this way?
options: So students can overload gradually and avoid injury
Because the teacher does not want students improving too quickly
Because running over five minutes is unsafe for teenagers
So that everyone finishes the session at exactly the same time
questions.explanation_en: This is the progressive overload principle: only increase the amount a little at a time, allowing your body to adapt and avoiding sudden increases that can cause muscle soreness and injury, as stated in the course notes with 'no sudden increase in volume or intensity'.
questions.source: Wednesday sport Remote Learning Week 4 / Week 5

questions.topic: Sport safety · Heat and sun protection
questions.stem: Which is the best preparation for an outdoor athletics carnival on a hot day?
options: Drink plenty of water and bring a hat and sun protection
Wear an extra jumper so you sweat more and lose weight
Avoid drinking until after your last event
Wear brand new spikes you have never worn before
questions.explanation_en: According to the course notice, it's essential to bring enough water, protect yourself from the sun, and wear a hat, as intentionally drinking less water increases the risk of heatstroke and cramps, and new spiked shoes can cause blisters, so you shouldn't wear them for the first time on competition day.
questions.source: Bally Boys school athletics carnival permission note.doc（What to bring）

questions.stem: In the Week 6 strength routine, students complete 'AMRAP in 20 minutes'. What does AMRAP mean?
options: As many reps or rounds as possible in the set time
A mandatory rest period after every repetition
A measured running and pacing test over a set distance
Alternating muscle recovery with performance work
questions.explanation_en: AMRAP means as many reps/rounds as possible, which involves completing as many cycles as possible within the given time (5 superman poses, 10 push-ups, 15 squats), and stopping once the time is up.

questions.stem: How is the age champion decided at the swimming carnival?
options: By the highest aggregate point score across events
By winning a single 50m freestyle race on the day
By a vote of all teachers at the end of the carnival
By the fastest 100m time recorded on the day
questions.explanation_en: The age group champion is determined by the highest cumulative score across all events, so achieving multiple placings is more beneficial than winning a single event, as a single event win only earns a single score.

questions.stem: During a 25-minute run a student feels a sharp pain in his hamstring. Describe what he should do and explain why continuing to run would be risky.
questions.answer: He should stop running immediately, tell the teacher or coach, and get the injury assessed and treated with rest, ice, compression and elevation before returning to play. Continuing to run is risky because a strained muscle can tear further, causing a much longer recovery, and pain is a warning sign that should never be pushed through.
questions.explanation_en: Scoring points require 'immediate stop + reporting to the teacher/coach + RICER treatment', and explaining that continuing to run will worsen the injury and prolong the recovery period, as running through the pain is the most common incorrect choice.
questions.source: School XC Program 2025 (event safety guidelines) + syllabus knowledge (RICER first-aid principles)

criteria.t: States that he should stop running immediately
States that he should tell the teacher or coach and have the injury assessed
Describes treating it with rest, ice, compression and elevation before returning to play
Explains the risk: a strained muscle can tear further, causing a much longer recovery, and pain is a warning sign that must not be pushed through

questions.stem: Using the Wednesday Sport program as an example, explain what progressive overload means and why it is safer than suddenly training much harder.
questions.answer: Progressive overload means gradually increasing the training demand over time, for example moving from a 45-minute walk with bodyweight exercises to jogging 4 minutes and walking 1 minute, and eventually to a continuous 25-minute run. It is safer because each small increase gives the body time to adapt, whereas a sudden jump in volume or intensity causes muscle soreness and greatly increases the risk of injury.
questions.explanation_en: The definition, specific examples from the materials, and 'why it's safer' must all be included, so simply writing 'gradually increase the amount' without providing examples or explaining the risk of injury will not earn full marks.
questions.source: Wednesday Sport Remote Learning Week 1–6（train progressions and Week 6 25-minute run）

criteria.t: Defines progressive overload as gradually increasing the training demand over time
Gives the program example: from a 45-minute walk with bodyweight exercises to jogging 4 minutes and walking 1 minute, then a continuous 25-minute run
Explains that each small increase gives the body time to adapt
Contrasts this with a sudden jump in volume or intensity, which causes muscle soreness and greatly increases the risk of injury

questions.stem: Explain why a signed permission note and accurate medical information are required before a student competes in a representative sport event, and give one example of a safety rule from the school's sport documents.
questions.answer: A permission note shows that a parent or guardian knows the event details and accepts that some risk is inherent in sport, and medical information lets staff plan first aid and manage conditions such as asthma or allergy on the day. One example of a safety rule is that a correctly fitted mouthguard is mandatory in all rugby league games and training sessions.
questions.explanation_en: There are two questions: one is 'parental informed consent + school preparedness for first aid and knowledge of medical history', and the other is citing a genuine regulation (such as mandatory mouthguards or bringing water and sun protection), as only writing 'school requires a signature' without explaining the reason will result in lost points.
questions.source: Rugby_League_Trials_permission_note.docx；Bally Boys school athletics carnival permission note.doc

criteria.t: Explains that a permission note shows a parent or guardian knows the event details and accepts that some risk is inherent in sport
Explains that accurate medical information lets staff plan first aid and manage conditions such as asthma or allergy on the day
Gives one accurate safety rule from the school's sport documents, such as a correctly fitted mouthguard being mandatory in rugby league games and training
